newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria asks CA super board chief to stay on.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria asks CA super board chief to stay on.

text.p: Bank Austria said on Monday it had asked Creditanstalt's supervisory board chief to stay on after he offered his resignation following Bank Austria's move to take control of its rival.

"We have complete confidence in supervisory board president Walter Fremuth. Bank Austria will ask (him) to remain in his position after it has taken over the state's stake (in Creditanstalt)," the bank said in a brief statement.

Bank Austria paid 17.2 billion schillings for the state's 70 percent voting stake in the establishment bank and agreed to keep it independent for at least five years while giving a job guarantee to all of Creditanstalt's 9,800 employees.
Fremuth earlier told Austrian state radio that the bank may manage to keep its independence for more than five years if both partners could realise sufficient synergies on their own.
"The most important thing now is to make sure that one plus one will be more than two," he said.
A Creditanstalt spokesman said the bank had not yet heard from its new majority owner and was in the dark about Bank Austria's future strategy.
